source.title: Tracking Universal Features Through Fine-Tuning and Model Merging

record.tranche_reason: The study uses sparse autoencoders and activation-pattern comparisons to examine whether identifiable features can be recovered and tracked in small language models, a conceptual test of indirect SAE-feature evidence. It does not test toy-model superposition itself.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE feature extraction, cross-model feature correlations, feature counts, and feature case studies. The interpolation accuracies are reported as a capability check, not as findings about the claim versions, so they are not included as rows. The 80% correlation threshold is a method choice, not a result row.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAEs as a tool to track feature persistence across fine-tuning and merging of one-layer LMs. Its results concern how features evolve between related models. They do not bear on whether models store features in superposition (V1–V3, V6). They also do not test whether SAE features are complete or canonical units of one model (V5). Loss of cross-model correspondence after fine-tuning can reflect real model change rather than dictionary instability. The SAE quality figures (L0 25–35, explained loss >88%) are reported only as a training check, so there is no V4 test either. Record as fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also conclude that slerp merging maintains parent-model features. They say features are diluted by fine-tuning and merging and correlate less well than for identically trained models. They claim their SAEs extract the same universal feature across models, reinforcing Bricken et al.'s extraction universality.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SAE extraction, feature-pattern correlations, fine-tuning, and spherical linear interpolation to study feature evolution; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature persistence is defined using an 80% activation-pattern correlation threshold, selected after manual inspection. The study compares distinct fine-tuning domains and a merged checkpoint.

fits_no_version.finding: In one-layer LMs, very few SAE features persist through fine-tuning to new domains (959 of 16,384 into either child). Merging by slerp retains parent features (1,210 traced: 729 emerged in fine-tuning, 481 from the base). Persisting features are mostly punctuation, formatting or code-related.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE-extracted features largely do not persist (by >80% activation correlation) across domain fine-tuning, while weight merging preserves parent features.

record.code_released: Code and weights promised upon publication; URL not stated
record.problems: The study uses one-layer small models and a limited set of domains. Feature persistence depends on an 80% correlation threshold chosen after manual inspection. The paper notes that the experiments cover just under half a billion tokens and may not capture larger, more diverse corpora.

untested.parts: All parts: no toy model, no geometry, no sparsity transition.
All parts: polysemanticity and capacity are not examined.
There is no test of feature spread across neurons or of SAE recovery as evidence of superposition. SAE quality metrics are a training check only.
Completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, and canonicity of SAE features within a model are not tested. Only cross-model correspondence after fine-tuning and merging is measured.

missing.what: SAE quality: mean L0 25–35, MSE <0.0067, explained loss >88%, 16× expansion. Potential V4 context if the study were treated as testing recovery.
Shares of persisting features by content: 20% punctuation, 5% formatting along BabyPython→Lua→LuaStories.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests V4/V5' rests on SAEs recovering interpretable features and on cross-model persistence. These concern feature evolution between different models, not superposition or the canonicity of dictionary features within a model. The persistence threshold of 80% was chosen by manual inspection. The case-study features are hand-selected. There are no controls, such as a seed-varied SAE on the same model, to separate SAE instability from real model change.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity arises from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
The study uses small one-layer language models and tests SAE-extracted features; it does not measure feature spread across neurons in large LLMs or directly test SAE recovery in frontier models.
The study examines feature correspondence across fine-tuning and merging, but does not establish that SAE features are complete, canonical units within a model.
Whether the represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The tested small one-layer models and the studied SAE features
reader_labels.reason: The authors recover interpretable SAE features, including a variable-assignment feature tracked across models; the reported assignment-feature correlations and log-likelihood proxies support feature recovery in this setting (R5-R9).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Feature correspondence through the tested fine-tuning and merging changes
reader_labels.reason: Feature persistence is not general across these changes: most base-model features disappear, while the exception example has only 40.81% cross-model correlation, below the stated persistence threshold (R1, R10).
